text: The primary and secondary valencies of cobalt respectively in $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{5}\mathrm{Cl}]\mathrm{Cl}_{2}$ are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In Werner's theory the primary valency of the metal equals its oxidation state and the secondary valency equals its coordination number.

The complex ion is $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{5}\mathrm{Cl}]{}^{2+}$; with x as the oxidation state of Co,

$x+5(0)+(-1)=+2\Rightarrow x=+3$

So the primary valency is 3: two chlorides are ionisable counter-ions, and the coordinated chloride satisfies one primary and one secondary valency at the same time.

Five $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ and one $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ are bonded to Co, so the secondary valency (coordination number) is 6.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

solution.body:
In 3-(hydroxymethyl)phenol, the benzylic $-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}$ is an alcoholic group: it is protonated by HBr and replaced by bromide, giving 3-(bromomethyl)phenol as A. The phenolic $-\mathrm{OH}$ is not replaced, because the aryl $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}$ bond has partial double-bond character and an aryl cation does not form.

In 3-methoxyphenol, hot HBr cleaves the aryl methyl ether: $\mathrm{Br}{}^{-}$ attacks the protonated ether at the methyl carbon, so the $\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ bond breaks (not the aryl $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}$ bond), giving $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{Br}$ and a second phenolic $-\mathrm{OH}$. B is benzene-1,3-diol (resorcinol).


[IMG]

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
Assertion A : Hydrolysis of an alkyl chloride is a slow reaction but in the presence of NaI, the rate of the hydrolysis increases.

Reason R : I${}^{-}$ is a good nucleophile as well as a good leaving group.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Hydrolysis of an alkyl chloride is slow because $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ is only a moderate leaving group and water is a weak nucleophile.

$\mathrm{I}{}^{-}$ is large and highly polarisable, so it is a strong nucleophile and rapidly displaces chloride: $\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{Cl}+\mathrm{I}{}^{-}\longrightarrow \mathrm{R}-\mathrm{I}+\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$.

$\mathrm{I}{}^{-}$ is also an excellent leaving group (weakest C–X bond, weakest base among halides), so the alkyl iodide is hydrolysed much faster: $\mathrm{R}-\mathrm{I}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}\longrightarrow \mathrm{R}-\mathrm{OH}+\mathrm{H}{}^{+}+\mathrm{I}{}^{-}$.

The $\mathrm{I}{}^{-}$ is regenerated and acts as a catalyst; this dual role, stated in R, is exactly why the rate increases in A.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

In the following given reaction, 'A' is


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$ from HBr adds to the terminal $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ (Markovnikov), giving the tertiary carbocation $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{C}{}^{+}$ attached to the cyclobutane ring.

A ring C–C bond migrates to this cationic carbon (ring expansion), relieving the strain of the four-membered ring. The cationic carbon becomes a cyclopentane ring carbon carrying both methyl groups, and the positive charge moves to the neighbouring ring carbon (secondary 2,2-dimethylcyclopentyl cation).

A 1,2-methyl shift from the adjacent $\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}$ carbon converts this secondary cation into the more stable tertiary 1,2-dimethylcyclopentyl cation.

$\mathrm{Br}{}^{-}$ attacks the tertiary carbon, giving 1-bromo-1,2-dimethylcyclopentane.


[IMG]

A further expansion to a six-membered ring does not occur, because the positive charge is now on a ring carbon and no ring bond lies next to an exocyclic cationic carbon.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
Compound (X) undergoes following sequence of reactions to give the Lactone (Y).


[IMG]


Compound (X) is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Lactone Y is 3-hydroxy-4,4-dimethyloxolan-2-one: the ring $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}$ carbon is bonded to a $\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})$ carbon, then a $\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}$ carbon, then a $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ carbon joined to the ring oxygen. It is the cyclic ester of 2,4-dihydroxy-3,3-dimethylbutanoic acid, $\mathrm{HOCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})\mathrm{COOH}$.

X is 2-methylpropanal, $(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{CHCHO}$. Its single $α$-hydrogen lets KOH form the enolate, which adds to HCHO (crossed aldol) to give 3-hydroxy-2,2-dimethylpropanal:

$(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{CHCHO}+\mathrm{HCHO}{}^{\mathrm{KOH}}\mathrm{HOCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{CHO}$

Cyanide adds to the aldehyde to form the cyanohydrin; $\mathrm{H}{}_{3}\mathrm{O}{}^{+}$ hydrolyses $-\mathrm{CN}$ to $-\mathrm{COOH}$, and the resulting 4-hydroxy acid closes to the five-membered lactone:

$\mathrm{HOCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{CHO}{}^{\mathrm{KCN}}\mathrm{HOCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})\mathrm{CN}{}^{\mathrm{H}{}_{3}\mathrm{O}{}^{+}}\mathrm{HOCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})\mathrm{COOH}\longrightarrow \mathrm{Y}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$


[IMG]

Compound (C) is the aldol product itself; having no $α$-hydrogen, it would only undergo a crossed Cannizzaro reaction with HCHO and KOH, and the straight-chain aldehydes (B) and (D) cannot supply the gem-dimethyl carbon of Y.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text:
Order of Covalent bond;

$\mathrm{A}.\mathrm{KF}>\mathrm{KI};\mathrm{LiF}>\mathrm{KF}$

$\mathrm{B}.\mathrm{KF}<\mathrm{KI};\mathrm{LiF}>\mathrm{KF}$

$\mathrm{C}.\mathrm{SnCl}_{4}>\mathrm{SnCl}_{2};\mathrm{CuCl}>\mathrm{NaCl}$

$\mathrm{D}.\mathrm{LiF}>\mathrm{KF};\mathrm{CuCl}<\mathrm{NaCl}$

$\mathrm{E}.\mathrm{KF}<\mathrm{KI};\mathrm{CuCl}>\mathrm{NaCl}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
By Fajans' rules, covalent character rises with the polarising power of the cation (higher charge, smaller size, or an 18-electron outer shell) and with the size and polarisability of the anion.

$\mathrm{KF}<\mathrm{KI}$ because $\mathrm{I}{}^{-}$ is far larger and more polarisable than $\mathrm{F}{}^{-}$, and $\mathrm{LiF}>\mathrm{KF}$ because $\mathrm{Li}{}^{+}$ is much smaller than $\mathrm{K}{}^{+}$; so A is incorrect and B is correct.

$\mathrm{SnCl}{}_{4}>\mathrm{SnCl}{}_{2}$ because $\mathrm{Sn}{}^{4+}$ has higher charge and smaller size than $\mathrm{Sn}{}^{2+}$.

$\mathrm{CuCl}>\mathrm{NaCl}$ because $\mathrm{Cu}{}^{+}$ has an 18-electron outer shell whose $d$ electrons shield the nucleus poorly, so it polarises $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ far more than $\mathrm{Na}{}^{+}$ with its noble-gas shell; so C is correct, D is incorrect and E is correct.

The correct statements are B, C and E.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text:
Increasing order of stability of the resonance structures is :


[IMG]


Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
All four are resonance structures of $\mathrm{OHC}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$; each carries one positive and one negative charge, so stability depends on complete octets and on whether each charge sits next to a group that stabilises it.

In D every atom has a complete octet: the positive charge is on nitrogen as $=\mathrm{N}{}^{+}\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$ and the negative charge is on the carbon next to $\mathrm{CHO}$, where it is delocalised onto the carbonyl oxygen. D is the most stable.

In B the carbanion is next to the electron-withdrawing $\mathrm{CHO}$ and the carbocation is next to the lone pair of $\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$, so both charges are stabilised, but the cationic carbon has only a sextet.

In A the carbocation is next to the electron-withdrawing $\mathrm{CHO}$ and the carbanion is next to the lone pair of $\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$, so both charges are destabilised, and one carbon has only a sextet.

In C the positive charge is on the electronegative oxygen, which has only one bond and an incomplete octet, and the negative charge is next to $\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$; C is the least stable.

Increasing order of stability: $\text{C}<\text{A}<\text{B}<\text{D}$.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

text:
When $\mathrm{Fe}_{0.93}\mathrm{O}$ is heated in presence of oxygen, it converts to $\mathrm{Fe}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$. The number of correct statement/s from the following is $________$

A. The equivalent weight of $\mathrm{Fe}_{0.93}\mathrm{O}$ is $\frac{\mathrm{Molecular}\mathrm{weight}}{0.79}$

B. The number of moles of Fe${}^{2+}$ and Fe${}^{3+}$ in 1 mole of $\mathrm{Fe}_{0.93}\mathrm{O}$ is 0.79 and 0.14 respectively

C. $\mathrm{Fe}_{0.93}\mathrm{O}$ is metal deficient with lattice comprising of cubic closed packed arrangement of O${}^{2-}$ ions

D. The % composition of Fe${}^{2+}$ and Fe${}^{3+}$ in $\mathrm{Fe}_{0.93}\mathrm{O}$ is 85% and 15% respectively
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the number of $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ ions be $x$ and number of $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ ions be $0.93-x$.

According to the charge neutrality,

$\begin{array}{l} 2x+3(0.93-x)=2\Rightarrow 2x-3x+2.79=2\Rightarrow x=0.79 \\  \\ \mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\text{ion}=x=0.79 \\  \\ \mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\text{ion}=0.93-x=0.93-0.79=0.14 \\  \\ %\text{of}\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\text{ion}=\dfrac{0.79}{0.93}\times 100=84.95%\approx 85% \\  \\ %\text{of}\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\text{ion}=\dfrac{0.14}{0.93}\times 100=15.05% \end{array}$

As it is a metal deficiency defect, 

so, 1 mol of $\mathrm{Fe}_{0.93}\mathrm{O}$ contains $1\mathrm{mol}$ of oxide ions and $0.93\mathrm{mol}$ of iron ions as $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$.

So, moles of $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}=0.79$

and moles of $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}=0.14$

$\text{The equivalent weight}=\frac{\text{Molecular weight}}{n\text{-factor}}$

$Fe^{2+}\to Fe^{3+}+e^{-}$

For one $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+},n$-factor $=1$

$\therefore$ For $0.79\mathrm{Fe}^{2+},n$-factor $=0.79$

Out of $0.93\mathrm{mol}$, there are $0.79\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ ions are present.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:

The secondary benzylic Cl gives a resonance-stabilised benzylic carbocation, and the tertiary Cl on the side chain gives a tertiary carbocation stabilised by hyperconjugation; both ionise and give AgCl.

The vinylic Cl and the aryl Cl are bonded to $sp^{2}$ carbons; their C–Cl bonds have partial double-bond character through resonance, and vinyl or aryl cations are highly unstable, so these two Cl atoms do not react.

Each mole of the compound therefore gives 2 mol of AgCl.

Hence, the answer is 2.

text: The dissociation constant of acetic acid is $x\times 10^{-5}$. When 25 mL of 0.2 $\mathrm{M}\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{COONa}$ solution is mixed with 25 mL of 0.02 $\mathrm{M}\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{COOH}$ solution, the pH of the resultant solution is found to be equal to 5. solution.body:
To find the dissociation constant of acetic acid, we use the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation for the given system and conditions. The equation is as follows:

$\text{pH}=\text{pK}_{\text{a}}+\log \left (\frac{[\text{CH}_{3}\text{COO}^{-}]}{[\text{CH}_{3}\text{COOH}]}\right )$

In the solution mixture:

We have 25 mL of 0.2 M $\text{CH}_{3}\text{COONa}$ and 25 mL of 0.02 M $\text{CH}_{3}\text{COOH}$.

The concentration ratio $\left (\frac{[\text{CH}_{3}\text{COONa}]}{[\text{CH}_{3}\text{COOH}]}\right )$ becomes $\frac{25\times 0.2}{25\times 0.02}=10$.

Given that the pH of the solution is 5, we substitute into the equation:

$5=\text{pK}_{\text{a}}+\log 10$

Since $\log 10=1$, we solve for $\text{pK}_{\text{a}}$:

$5=\text{pK}_{\text{a}}+1\Rightarrow \text{pK}_{\text{a}}=4$

Converting from $\text{pK}_{\text{a}}$ to $K_{\text{a}}$, we use:

$K_{\text{a}}=10^{-\text{pK}_{\text{a}}}=10^{-4}$

Thus, since the dissociation constant $K_{\text{a}}$ is given as $x\times 10^{-5}$, compare:

$10^{-4}=10\times 10^{-5}$

Therefore, $x=10$.

text:
At 298 K, a 1 litre solution containing 10 mmol of $\mathrm{C}\mathrm{r}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-}$ and 100 mmol of $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$ shows a pH of 3.0.

Given : $\mathrm{C}\mathrm{r}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-}\to \mathrm{C}\mathrm{r}^{3+};\mathrm{E}^{\circ }=1.330$V

and $\frac{2.303\mathrm{RT}}{F}=0.059$ V

The potential for the half cell reaction is $x\times 10^{-3}$ V. The value of $x$ is $__________$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body: $\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{Cr}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-}+14\mathrm{H}^{+}+6\mathrm{e}^{-}\to 2\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}+7\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O} \\  \\ \mathrm{E}=1.33-\dfrac{0.059}{6}\log \dfrac{(0.1)^{2}}{\left (10^{-2}\right )\left (10^{-3}\right )^{14}} \\  \\ \mathrm{E}=1.33-\dfrac{0.059}{6}\times 42=0.917 \\  \\ \mathrm{E}=917\times 10^{-3} \\  \\ \mathrm{x}=917 \end{array}$

text: If wavelength of the first line of the Paschen series of hydrogen atom is 720 nm, then the wavelength of the second line of this series is $_________ nm. ($Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 24th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\frac{1}{720}=R\times \left (\frac{1}{9}-\frac{1}{16}\right )$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow R=\dfrac{9\times 16}{720\times 7} \\  \\ \dfrac{1}{λ^{'}}=\dfrac{9\times 16}{720\times 7}\times \left (\dfrac{1}{9}-\dfrac{1}{25}\right ) \\  \\ λ^{'}=492.18\mathrm{nm} \\  \\ λ^{'}=492\mathrm{nm}\text{(nearest integer)} \end{array}$
